subject: Terms and seat-mapping: QuantArc transition economics and onboarding credits
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam@quantarc.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quantarc.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: QuantArc vendor swap — credit structure & seat mapping questions

Hi Grace / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — QuantArc's engineering and ops teams were impressed with the latency profiles. Before we advance to redlines, Procurement has a few open items on economics that I wanted to summarize so we can converge quickly: 

- We need a comparable TCO to our incumbent (HyperScale AI). Can you match their effective per-request unit at our current volume profile?
- Seat mapping: we currently bill a mixture of named seats + consumption. How would Redwood map our 1,200 named seats into your packaging? Any conversion rules and minimums?
- Onboarding credits: we typically require an implementation credit to soften the first 90 days while we ramp traffic. QuantArc has asked for a $75k onboarding credit.
- Egress & retention: separate line items — we prefer a single blended price.

Can you send a short worked example showing the three models (flat seats, consumption reservation, hybrid commit+overage) for our current monthly profile? If you can include an estimate of the month-1 effective unit cost after credits that would be great.

Ellie (procurement) is copied — she will handle the PO and contract logistics.

Best,
Sam
Sam Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantArc
Attachment: quantarc_mop_v0.csv (csv)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam@quantarc.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@quantarc.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QuantArc vendor swap — credit structure & seat mapping questions

Hi Sam — great to hear the team liked the demo. I pushed a concise workbook (attached) with the worked examples you asked for — three scenarios for your current profile:

1) Named-seat conversion: we map 1 named seat = 1 seat license; for high-volume agents we recommend a discounted seat bucket. Effective per-request calculated at 1,200 seats and your current monthly token utilization is on sheet "Seats".

2) Reservation (commit + overage): a 6-month committed throughput reservation priced at a 25% discount to our list yields predictable unit economics; overages billed at a slightly higher unit rate.

3) Hybrid (reserve core capacity + variable burst): recommended for mixed workloads — we show a 3-month ramp with $40k onboarding credit applied to month 1.

Regarding your $75k ask — to bridge to list we can offer $50k onboarding credit + a targeted 10% first-year usage rebate structured as a quarterly bill credit. That preserves our margin while delivering a clear month-1 dollar impact.

On egress / retention: we can provide a blended add-on — I'll include both a blended price and a separate egress line in the final SOW so Procurement can compare apples-to-apples.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm which scenario you'd like modeled (Seats / Reservation / Hybrid) by EOD Friday so we can finalize pricing.
- If you want the full SOW we can produce a draft for signatures within 3 business days after scenario selection.

Attached: quantarc_onboarding_worksheet_v1.xlsx; redwood-terms-summary-QARC-4521.pdf

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference - Developer-first inference platform
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: QuantArc deal guardrails and acceptable concession range

Grace / Marissa — quick internal note after reviewing Grace's proposed structure and the attached workbook. My position and asks: 

- Margin floor: we should not go below a 22% blended gross margin for the first 12 months on QARC-4521 unless Legal secures stronger indemnities.
- Onboarding credit: $50k + 10% usage rebate is acceptable as a standard play. If Procurement insists on $75k we can trade a shorter SLA commitment window (move SLA uptime to 99.5% for first 3 months) or require a 12-month minimum commit instead of 6 months.
- Seat mapping: allow a 10% cushion for overage conversion (i.e., convert every 10 high-utilization seats into 1 additional reserved slot) — document in the SOW to avoid disputes.

Please bake these guardrails into the pricing memo before it goes out. Also request Legal to prepare the SOW template with explicit billing cadence and rollback language for seat de-duplication.

Connor
Director, Commercial Operations
From: Sam Rivera <sam@quantarc.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Ellie Park <ellie.park@quantarc.com>, procurement@quantarc.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QuantArc vendor swap — credit structure & seat mapping questions

Grace — thanks for the clear options and the worksheet. QuantArc's procurement team reviewed and we want to move forward with the Hybrid model you described but with two small asks: 

1) Increase the onboarding credit to $60k (we can meet you halfway on the $50k number).
2) Add a 90-day SLA rollback clause that allows us to request a performance remediation credit if p50 latency deviates more than 2x baseline during the first 90 days.

If Redwood can accept those two tweaks, I can have Ellie circulate a PO and the legal team will push an expedited DocuSign for signatures. We expect a go-live target in mid-September if we sign next week.

Sam
Head of Platform Engineering, QuantArc
Attachment: procurement-intent-QuantArc.pdf (pdf)
